headline: Meeting of Prime Minister with the President of the Russian Federation
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Meeting of Prime Minister with the President of the Russian Federation

31 AUG 2026 9:49PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today met the President of the Russian Federation, H.E. Vladimir Putin, in Bishkek, on the margins of the 26th SCO Summit. This was their first meeting this year. The two leaders had earlier met in Delhi for the 23rd Annual Summit in December 2025.

The two leaders reviewed progress in bilateral cooperation in a range of fields, including political, economic, defence, energy, space, mobility and people-to-people ties. They welcomed the outcome of the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic and Cultural matters, which was held on 24 August 2026 in Moscow.

The leaders exchanged views on India-Russia engagement in the multilateral arena, in particular in BRICS under India’s Chairship for 2026. They also shared perspectives on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, including the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region which have impacted maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers. Prime Minister reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy was the way forward in resolving conflicts.

The two leaders agreed to remain engaged to further strengthen the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between the two countries, which continues to register significant growth and has shown resilience in the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainties.

Prime Minister stated that he looks forward to welcoming President Putin in India for the 18th BRICS Summit on 12-13 September 2026.

headline: DRI seizes over 42 kg foreign-origin gold worth more than RS. 65 crore in crackdown on gold smuggling
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

DRI seizes over 42 kg foreign-origin gold worth more than RS. 65 crore in crackdown on gold smuggling

25 persons arrested in multiple intelligence-led operations across Kolkata, Mumbai, Kerala and other locations

31 AUG 2026 9:30PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on organised gold smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has, in a series of intelligence-led operations across the country in recent days, seized over 42 kg foreign-origin gold, and around 10 kg Silver, collectively valued at more than Rs. 65 crore, and arrested 25 persons including 5 foreign nationals.

The operations have exposed diverse and sophisticated modus operandi, including concealment in specially fabricated vehicle cavities, body concealment, use of transit passengers and airport personnel, and smuggling through land and coastal routes.

Major operation at Mumbai Airport

On 28/29.08.26, DRI unearthed a well-organised syndicate involved in smuggling foreign-origin gold through Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai. The syndicate involved foreign nationals transiting through Mumbai from destinations including Dubai, Bangkok and Male, as well as an airport staff member facilitating clandestine removal of the smuggled gold at Mumbai. A total of 16 capsules containing 6.85 kg of 24-carat gold dust in wax form, were recovered and seized.

6.85 kg gold in wax form seized at Mumbai airport

The operation resulted in the arrest of six persons, comprising of five foreign nationals who were transiting through Mumbai and one airport staff member. The operation once again highlights that organised networks are increasingly exploiting transit routes and airport personnel for clandestine removal of smuggled gold.

Major seizures in Kolkata/West Bengal

On 29,08,26, in two separate intelligence-led operations at NSCBI Airport, Kolkata, officers of DRI intercepted two passengers travelling from Bangkok and Dubai respectively, suspected to be part of gold-smuggling syndicates.

15.61 kg gold seized by DRI in coordination with BSF in Nadia district

In a case involving two passengers coming from Dubai, 4.87 kg gold was recovered after semi-solid gold-containing paste was found concealed in the undergarments and jeans of two passengers. The material was melted and the extracted gold in bar form was seized. Both passengers were arrested under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

In another case, involving flight coming from Bangkok, 3.36 kg foreign-origin gold was recovered in the form of 11 raw chains from one passenger, which had allegedly been handed over to him by the second passenger for crossing the Green Channel. Both passengers were arrested.

On the same day, in another case, the DRI seized 125 pieces of foreign-origin gold bars weighing 15.61 kg. It was recovered by troops of Border Security Force (BSF), at BOP Tungi from a woman during a surprise search of her residential premise in Banpur village, Nadia district. During investigation by DRI, the woman admitted to her involvement in the alleged smuggling activity along with the men of the house. The woman was arrested under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

1.74 kg gold seized by DRI in coordination with BSF

Two more seizures in Kerala

In two separate operations in Kerala on 29.08.2026, DRI Cochin Zonal Unit and its Calicut Regional Unit intercepted passengers arriving from Ras Al Khaimah and Jeddah respectively. At Cochin International Airport, 1.78 kg gold, was extracted from two packets of gold in compound form concealed on the person of a passenger arriving from Ras Al Khaimah; the passenger was arrested.

At Calicut International Airport, DRI officers, along with the Air Intelligence Unit, detected 549 grams of 24-carat foreign-origin gold, concealed in especially created cavities inside the heavy alloy portion of an iron box carried by a passenger arriving from Jeddah. The gold was seized under the Customs Act,1962 and the passenger was arrested.

Earlier in the week, on 26–27.08.2026, DRI, in coordination with BSF, also effected several significant seizures of foreign-origin gold along the Indo-Bangladesh border, The officers of DRI Unit seized 935 grams and 1.74 kg foreign-origin gold in two separate operations, resulting in the arrest of one person in each case.

In another operation in Kolkata, 1.48 kg foreign-origin (FO) gold in paste form, allegedly smuggled from Thailand, was recovered by officers of DRI from four persons. who were found to be carrying smuggled FO Gold in paste form in 5 capsules secreted in their rectum/ body during aa domestic road trip. All four persons and their handler were arrested.

In Guwahati, DRI seized 3.84 kg foreign-origin gold bars allegedly smuggled through the Indo-Bangladesh border in the Tripura sector and arrested two persons including a lady.

Further, in Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu, DRI seized 1.360 kg foreign-origin gold and 9.99 kg foreign-origin silver, allegedly smuggled through the coastal route from Sri Lanka, and arrested three persons.

Seized gold and silver at Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu

DRI's intelligence-led and coordinated enforcement actions continue to disrupt these networks at multiple stages of the smuggling chain and prevent the illicit movement of precious metals into the country.

headline: Chhattisgarh Strengthens Its Role in India’s Critical Mineral Ecosystem; CM Vishnu Deo Sai Highlights State’s Commitment to Mineral Development
fullText:
Ministry of Mines

Chhattisgarh Strengthens Its Role in India’s Critical Mineral Ecosystem; CM Vishnu Deo Sai Highlights State’s Commitment to Mineral Development

MoS Satish Chandra Dubey Calls for Greater Industry Participation

Five mineral blocks from Chhattisgarh included in the 8th Tranche of Critical & Strategic Mineral Blocks

31 AUG 2026 9:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Mines organised a Roadshow on the 8th Tranche of Auction of Critical and Strategic Mineral Blocks in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, today. The programme was attended by the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, Shri Vishnu Deo Sai, as the Chief Guest, and Hon’ble Minister of State for Coal and Mines, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey. Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu, and Shri Saurabh Singh, Chairman, CMDC, were also present, along with senior officials, industry representatives and other stakeholders.

Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai highlighted Chhattisgarh’s rich mineral resources and the State’s important role in India’s mining and industrial development. He emphasised the need to unlock the State’s mineral potential through greater investment, faster development of mineral resources and close coordination between the Centre and the State. He assured stakeholders of the State Government’s commitment to facilitating investment and creating a conducive environment for sustainable mineral development.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Minister of State for Coal and Mines, highlighted the strategic importance of critical and strategic minerals for India’s economic growth, industrial development, clean energy transition and emerging technologies. He emphasised the need to accelerate exploration and development of these resources, while encouraging greater participation from industry and investors. He said that stronger domestic capabilities across the mineral value chain would play an important role in strengthening India’s mineral security and advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat

Shri Tokhan Sahu, Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, highlighted Chhattisgarh’s strong mining and industrial base and its potential to develop new mineral value chains. He emphasised that investments in critical minerals can drive new industrial growth centres, strengthen sustainable infrastructure and create opportunities for local communities. He noted that the State’s infrastructure, skilled workforce and institutional support provide a strong foundation for long-term investment.

Shri Saurabh Singh, Chairman, CMDC, invited investors to explore Chhattisgarh’s vast mineral potential and highlighted the State’s focus on faster operationalisation, transparent mining practices and technology-driven mineral monitoring. He also highlighted initiatives such as the TIN Portal for transparent benefit disbursement to tribal tin collectors and exploration of critical minerals such as Columbite.

Shri Keshav Chandra, Secretary, Ministry of Mines, said policy reforms, transparent auctions and faster operationalisation had strengthened India’s critical mineral ecosystem, with 56 of the 88 Critical and Strategic Mineral Blocks offered so far successfully auctioned. He said the 8th Tranche comprises 20 blocks, 17 Composite Licence and 3 Mining Lease, across nine States, covering Graphite, Rare Earth Elements, Rare Metals, Vanadium, Gallium, Titanium, Molybdenum, Tungsten, Potash, Phosphorite and Glauconite, of which five are in Chhattisgarh.

Shri Sandeep Kadam, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Mines, in his address, highlighted the importance of critical minerals for India’s economic growth, energy security and strategic industries. He stressed the need to move beyond mining towards processing, refining and value addition, along with faster operationalisation of auctioned blocks. He also called for stronger collaboration among the Centre, States and industry to build resilient domestic supply chains and a self-reliant critical mineral ecosystem.

The technical session opened with a presentation by Shri Pankaj Garg, DG, NMEDT, on the NMEDT Scheme for Partial Reimbursement of Exploration Expenses for Composite Licence Holders. Prospective bidders were then briefed in detail on the mineral blocks offered under the 8th Tranche and the auction framework by Shri Shrikant Sharma, HoD (Exploration), MECL, on the blocks and their potential; Shri Pratin Sharma, Assistant Vice President, SBICAPS, on the mineral auction process and tender document; and Shri Pushkar Hajela, Assistant Manager, MSTC, on the e-auction process. The session concluded with an interaction with prospective bidders, addressing their queries and providing clarifications on the auction process and related aspects.

The Roadshow reflects the Government’s continued commitment to accelerating mineral exploration, promoting investment and private-sector participation, and strengthen India’s critical mineral supply chains towards the vision of a self-reliant and mineral-secure India.

Following the Roadshow, a review meeting was held under the chairmanship of Shri Keshav Chandra, Secretary, Ministry of Mines, with mineral block allottees and preferred bidders to accelerate the early operationalisation of allocated blocks. Officials of the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, and the Government of Chhattisgarh reviewed the progress of the blocks, discussed key challenges and provided guidance for their timely resolution. The meeting also provided a platform for allottees to raise implementation-related issues and seek appropriate support, reinforcing the shared commitment towards faster project execution, increased domestic mineral production and strengthen India’s mineral supply chain.

headline: From Vulnerability to Recovery and Self-Reliance: Yogesh Rebuilds His Life with DDAC Support
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Vulnerability to Recovery and Self-Reliance: Yogesh Rebuilds His Life with DDAC Support

31 AUG 2026 8:53PM by PIB Delhi

For individuals living in vulnerable circumstances, timely outreach, treatment and rehabilitation support can create a pathway towards recovery, dignity and self-reliance. Such assistance can also help families overcome emotional distress and rebuild trust.

Demonstrating the impact of community outreach and rehabilitation support, Yogesh (name changed), a 35-year-old beneficiary from Udaipur, Rajasthan, overcame a period of instability and progressed towards recovery, social reintegration and financial independence.

Yogesh was living in an unstable and conflict-ridden environment with limited emotional support from his family. Belonging to an economically vulnerable household living below the poverty line, he faced generational debt, irregular income and dependence on daily-wage work.

With no formal education, Yogesh had limited livelihood opportunities. He aspired to acquire a sustainable trade or skill that could help him secure stable employment and improve his quality of life. His family was also experiencing financial hardship and emotional distress and, due to limited awareness and social anxiety, often felt helpless in supporting him.

Yogesh received support on 5 October 2023 through Aarogya Sewa Sansthan, a District De-Addiction Centre (DDAC) in Udaipur. Through community outreach and counselling under the Scheme, he was identified and motivated to seek treatment.

He was admitted to a supported rehabilitation facility, where he underwent a structured and medically supervised detoxification process to safely manage withdrawal symptoms.

Group sessions formed an important part of his recovery. These sessions enabled beneficiaries to share their experiences, reduce feelings of isolation, and encourage mutual support and accountability throughout the recovery process.

The assistance extended beyond treatment and rehabilitation. Yogesh received support in identifying stable employment opportunities and guidance on government-supported self-employment initiatives and micro-financing opportunities for livelihood generation.

Following treatment and rehabilitation support, Yogesh successfully reintegrated into mainstream society. He regained the trust and respect of his family and community, helping him overcome social stigma.

Yogesh is now a full-time employee. He has transitioned from financial dependence to becoming a primary earning member of his family and contributes towards household expenses, debt repayment and overall family welfare.

The intervention brought meaningful changes not only to Yogesh's personal circumstances but also to his family environment. Stable employment and renewed social acceptance have enabled him to rebuild his life with greater confidence and responsibility.

Yogesh's journey demonstrates how community outreach, counselling, medically supervised treatment, group support and livelihood guidance can work together to support sustained recovery and social reintegration.

From living in an unstable environment and depending on irregular daily-wage work, Yogesh has progressed towards stability, employment and self-reliance.

Through timely support from Aarogya Sewa Sansthan, Yogesh was able to overcome isolation, regain the confidence of his family and community, and assume responsibility as a primary earning member. His journey reflects the role of structured rehabilitation and livelihood support in restoring dignity and strengthening family welfare.

headline: Department of Telecommunications Cautions Citizens against IMEI Tampering and Misuse of Telecommunication Identifiers
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Department of Telecommunications Cautions Citizens against IMEI Tampering and Misuse of Telecommunication Identifiers

IMEI Tampering and Telecom Identifier Misuse May Attract Up to Three Years’ Imprisonment and ₹50 Lakh Fine

Citizens advised to use the Sanchar Saathi Portal and Mobile App to verify and secure their mobile connections and handsets

31 AUG 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi

With the rapid expansion of mobile connectivity and digital services across India, the misuse of telecommunication identifiers, including the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number of mobile devices, has emerged as a matter of serious concern. Such misuse can compromise the safety of citizens and pose risks to the security and integrity of telecommunication networks. The Government of India has put in place stringent legal provisions to prevent tampering with and misuse of unique telecommunication identifiers.

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) reiterates that tampering with IMEI numbers or using devices with unauthorised or tampered telecommunication identifiers is a punishable offence under the Telecommunications Act, 2023 and the rules framed thereunder.

Key Legal Provisions

The Telecommunications Act, 2023 provides for stringent action against tampering with telecommunication identifiers, including the IMEI number of mobile handsets and other telecommunication devices.

Section 42(3)(c) prohibits tampering with telecommunication identifiers. Section 42(3)(e) prohibits obtaining Subscriber Identity Modules (SIMs) or telecommunication identifiers through fraud, cheating or impersonation.

Violations may attract imprisonment for up to three years, a fine of up to ₹50 lakh, or both. Such offences are cognizable and non-bailable under Section 42(7) of the Act. Under Section 42(6), persons who abet or promote the commission of such offences are also liable to the same punishment.

What Citizens Should Avoid

DoT advises citizens to refrain from:

Using, procuring or assembling devices such as modems, modules, SIM Boxes or other equipment with configurable or tampered IMEIs;

Procuring SIM cards through fake documents, fraud, cheating or impersonation;

Transferring, selling or handing over SIM cards obtained in their name to others who may misuse them; and

Using mobile applications, websites or any other means to modify Calling Line Identity (CLI) or other telecommunication identifiers.

Citizens should also note that procuring SIM cards in their own name and subsequently loaning, renting or muling of SIM for misuse in cyber fraud or any other unlawful activity may result in legal liability for the original subscriber.

Using devices with tampered IMEI numbers, obtaining SIM cards through fraudulent means, or transferring SIM cards to persons who misuse them can have serious legal consequences..

Verification and Reporting through Sanchar Saathi

Citizens are encouraged to remain vigilant and make use of the digital tools available through the Sanchar Saathi initiative to verify and secure their mobile handsets.

The IMEI details of a mobile handset can be verified through the Sanchar Saathi platform. The service enables citizens to check details such as the brand name, model name and manufacturer information associated with the device.

The Government has put in place robust measures to prevent the misuse of telecommunication resources and strengthen the safety and security of India's telecommunications ecosystem. Citizens can access various services available under the Sanchar Saathi initiative to verify and protect their mobile connections and devices.

Compliance with the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 and the rules framed thereunder is essential for preventing telecom-related fraud, protecting citizens and ensuring a safe, secure and trusted telecommunication environment.

Citizens are encouraged to visit the Sanchar Saathi Portal at www.sancharsaathi.gov.in or download the Sanchar Saathi Mobile App to access the various citizen-centric services available on the platform.

headline: NCSC Recommends Immediate Action and Arrest of Accused in Tarn Taran Case Within Five Days
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

NCSC Recommends Immediate Action and Arrest of Accused in Tarn Taran Case Within Five Days

Commission Reviews Alleged Derogatory Remarks Against Former Union Home Minister Late Shri Buta Singh

Police Protection Recommended for Petitioner, His Dependents in Delhi and Punjab

31 AUG 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi

The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), under the Chairmanship of Shri Kishor Makwana, Hon’ble Chairman, today conducted a hearing concerning the alleged derogatory remarks made by Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President Shri Amrinder Singh Raja Warring against former Union Home Minister Late Shri Buta Singh during an election campaign in Tarn Taran, Punjab.

Shri Harpreet Singh, DSP, Punjab, and Shri Gulzar Singh, DSP, EO & Cyber Crime, Punjab Police, appeared on behalf of the respondent authorities. The petitioner, Shri Sarabjot Singh, son of Late Shri Buta Singh, was also present during the hearing.

After hearing the parties and examining the material placed on record, the Commission expressed serious concern over the delay in completing the investigation, arresting the accused persons and submitting the Action Taken Report, despite specific recommendations issued during the previous hearing.

During the hearing held on 5th May 2026, the Commission had recommended that the investigation be completed within the stipulated period in accordance with the applicable rules.

Taking note of the petitioner’s complaint that he was receiving threatening calls from the alleged accused, the Commission had also directed that necessary protection be provided to the petitioner and his dependents under Section 15A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. An Action Taken Report was required to be submitted within 30 days. However, the Commission noted that the requisite report had not been received.

Taking serious note of the continuing delay, the Commission recommended that the authorities concerned initiate immediate action, in accordance with law, for the arrest of the accused persons and submit the status of the action taken to the Commission within five days.

The Commission further recommended that the investigation be completed expeditiously and the charge-sheet be filed before the competent court without further delay. It also called upon the competent authority to examine accountability for the delay in the investigation and arrest.

If any wilful neglect of duty by the investigating officer or officers is established, appropriate departmental action, including consideration of action under Section 4 of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, may be taken in accordance with law. The Commission has sought an Action Taken Report on its recommendations within 30 days.

The Commission also viewed the safety of the petitioner with particular seriousness. Ministry of Jal Shakti to host the First Departmental Summit under Hon'ble Prime Minister's Vision of Cooperative Federalism

31 AUG 2026 8:01PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards realizing the vision of Water Secure India and Viksit Bharat 2047, the Ministry of Jal Shakti will host the Departmental Summit on 1-2 September 2026 at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, New Delhi. The Summit is the first in a series of Departmental Summits envisioned by Hon'ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi as an innovative platform to strengthen cooperative federalism, foster collective ownership of national priorities, and accelerate outcomes through closer Centre-State collaboration.

Conceived in the spirit of Team India, the Departmental Summit model seeks to bring together political leadership and senior officials from the Union and State Governments to jointly deliberate on sectoral priorities, share good practices, address implementation challenges, and agree on time-bound actions for improved governance and service delivery. The Water Departmental Summit, being the first in this series, marks the beginning of a new approach to institutionalized collaboration between the Centre and States in pursuit of national development objectives.

The two-day Summit will focus on four key thematic pillars: timely implementation of water infrastructure projects; Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari-Catch the Rain; source sustainability of drinking water systems; and operation and maintenance of rural drinking water supply schemes under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. Discussions will cover project implementation, inter-agency coordination, water conservation, rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, digital monitoring, asset management, and strengthening community-led water governance.

The consultations are expected to culminate in concrete and time-bound outcomes, including accelerated completion of ongoing projects, enhanced public participation in water conservation, strengthened sustainability of drinking water sources, and improved accountability for reliable rural drinking water services. Participating States will share their experiences, challenges, best practices and consensus on agreed outcomes, reinforcing the spirit of cooperative federalism and shared responsibility.

Participating States will present the key outcomes and action plans emerging from the deliberations before Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during the valedictory session. The Hon'ble Prime Minister's guidance is expected to further strengthen the collective resolve of the Centre and States and provide momentum for the effective and timely implementation of the agreed action points.

headline: C-DOT Unveils 14 Indigenous Quantum Products to Strengthen Security of India’s Communication Networks
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

C-DOT Unveils 14 Indigenous Quantum Products to Strengthen Security of India’s Communication Networks

Quantum Product Series covers Quantum Key Distribution and Post-Quantum Cryptography solutions for secure and future-ready communications in quantum era

31 AUG 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT), the premier telecom R&D centre of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, unveiled 14 indigenous Quantum Products developed in the areas of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) during its 43rd Foundation Day celebrations in New Delhi.

The products unveiled include:

Q-AKSHAY CD: A compact, fibre-based Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) system based on Coherent One Way (COW) and Differential Phase Shift (DPS) protocols in a compact 1U size. It enables secure quantum key generation and distribution over fibre networks.

Q-AKSHAY MD: A fibre-based QKD system based on the Measurement Device Independent (MDI) protocol, offering enhanced security against vulnerabilities associated with measurement devices. It represents C-DOT’s next-generation approach to secure quantum key distribution.

C-SPD: A Single-Photon Detector, a critical sub-module used in quantum communication systems.

C-RD: A wideband RF driver designed to drive intensity and phase modulators used in quantum communication systems. It serves as a critical sub-module for enabling high-performance quantum communication applications.

Q-SETU: A quantum-safe encryptor designed to secure Layer 3 communications with a throughput of up to 80 Mbps. It incorporates National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms to protect data against emerging quantum-era threats.

Q-MAHASETU: A next-generation, commercial-grade quantum-safe encryptor supporting Layer 2/3 networks with throughput of up to 40 Gbps. It uses NIST PQC algorithms to provide high-speed, quantum-resistant protection for enterprise and critical communication networks.

Q-VIKRAM: A defence-grade quantum-safe encryptor providing up to 1 Gbps throughput for Layer 2/3 networks. It incorporates NIST PQC algorithms to provide enhanced protection for sensitive and strategic communications.

Q-AMOGH: A high-speed quantum-safe optical encryptor providing up to 200 Gbps throughput at Layer 1. Based on NIST PQC algorithms, it is designed to secure high-capacity optical communication links against emerging quantum threats.

Q-DARSHAN: A quantum-safe video IP phone incorporating NIST PQC algorithms to protect voice and video communications. It brings quantum-safe security directly into IP-based communication systems.

Q-VACHAN: A quantum-safe in-line node for IP phones using NIST PQC algorithms. It can upgrade existing IP phones with quantum security.

Q-RAQSHAK: A quantum-safe enterprise network solution designed to protect enterprise communications and network infrastructure. It incorporates NIST PQC algorithms to provide protection against current and future cryptographic threats.

Q-VAAYU: A quantum-safe wireless point-to-point network solution designed to secure wireless communication links. It uses NIST PQC algorithms to provide quantum-resistant security for wireless connectivity.

Q-VAJRA1000: A quantum-safe access node designed to upgrade existing communication networks with quantum security. It can support technologies such as GPON and wireless radios, enabling quantum-safe protection to be integrated into existing network infrastructure.

Q-PARAKRAM: A defence-grade quantum-safe encryptor providing up to 1 Gbps throughput for Layer 2/3 networks. It incorporates NIST PQC algorithms and other proprietary algorithms and is designed to provide robust quantum-resistant security for strategic and defence communications.

The Quantum Product Series brings together solutions for quantum-safe encryption, secure communications and critical components for quantum communication systems, catering to enterprise, telecom, wireless, optical, strategic and defence applications.The Quantum Product Series combines QKD technologies and PQC-based solutions to enable secure quantum key generation and distribution and are designed to protect communications against threats posed by future quantum computers. The quantum portfolio from C-DOT also spans specialised quantum communication components that can go in building quantum-safe security solutions for existing and next-generation networks by the eco system working in this area.

The products reflect the Centre’s focus on translating indigenous research and innovation into deployable solutions for securing India’s communication infrastructure in the emerging quantum era. These products have been developed to address emerging cybersecurity challenges associated with the advent of quantum computing and to strengthen the security and resilience of India’s communication networks.

A Quantum Product Series booklet, consolidating C-DOT’s indigenous quantum solutions, was also launched by the dignitaries. The booklet presents C-DOT’s work in QKD and PQC and highlights its efforts towards developing secure, resilient and future-ready communication technologies. Follow the link to access booklet:

headline: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw Pay Respect to Victims of the Flash Floods in Nepal
fullText:
Ministry of Railways

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw Pay Respect to Victims of the Flash Floods in Nepal

Chief Minister and Railway Minister Start Nepalganj Road-Nanpara-Bahraich Broad Gauge Rail Section in a Simple Programme

Four Trains Extended to Nepalganj Road, Boosting Development in Border Areas

31 AUG 2026 6:45PM by PIB Delhi

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, along with Union Minister for Railways, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw; Shri Jagdambika Pal, Member of Parliament from Domariyaganj; Dr. Anand Kumar Gond, Member of Parliament from Bahraich, and other dignitaries, inaugurated the gauge conversion and electrification of the Nepalganj Road-Nanpara-Bahraich rail section. The 56.15-km-long section has been converted to Broad Gauge and electrified at a cost of approximately ₹730 crore. Four existing train services were also extended up to Nepalganj Road. The programme began with a tribute to the victims of the recent floods in Nepal, with all those attending the programme observing two minutes of silence.

Expressing concern over the situation in neighbouring Nepal, the Union Minister said that India and Nepal share strong cultural ties. He expressed condolences to the families affected by the natural disaster in Nepal and said the Government of India is making every possible effort to provide assistance. Shri Vaishnaw said the Railways had also been making arrangements for passengers rescued from affected areas and reaching India. He said the Railways has arranged special coaches and other necessary facilities to help them reach their destinations. Shri Vaishnaw added that the Railway Board is working in coordination with railway zones, district and State authorities and the Ministry of External Affairs to facilitate the safe movement and return of passengers affected by the situation in Nepal.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath also expressed condolences over the recent natural disaster in Nepal. He said the tragedy had affected not only the friendly nation of Nepal but also people in several countries, including India, and conveyed his condolences to the families who have lost their members in the disaster.

Nepalganj Road-Nanpara-Bahraich Section Now Integrated into the Broad Gauge Railway Network

The Nepalganj Road-Nanpara-Bahraich metre-gauge rail section was originally constructed in 1886. With the completion of gauge conversion and electrification, the section has now become an integral part of the Broad Gauge railway network, providing improved connectivity to Bahraich, Risiya, Matera, Nanpara, Babaganj and Nepalganj Road stations.

Speaking about the railway section being inaugurated, Shri Vaishnaw said the conversion of the Nepalganj Road-Nanpara-Bahraich section is now connected to the wider railway network of the country. Shri Vaishnaw said the broad-gauge conversion programme is nearing completion across the country.

Extension of Long-Distance Train Services up to Nepalganj Road

To further enhance passenger connectivity, the Ministry of Railways has approved the extension of 14213/14214 Varanasi–Bahraich Express, 15132/15131 Varanasi City–Gorakhpur Express and two pairs of 75109/75110 and 75111/75112 Gonda–Bahraich train services up to Nepalganj Road.

With these services, passengers from Nepalganj Road and adjoining areas will get direct rail connectivity to Gonda, Gorakhpur, Varanasi and other major cities. The extension fulfills a long-standing demand of the people of the region and will significantly improve access to major urban and economic centres.The enhanced connectivity will also benefit people from neighbouring Nepal, particularly those travelling to and from the border region for employment, education, healthcare, trade and other purposes.

Shri Adityanath said the inauguration of the rail section and launch of four new train services marked the realisation of a decades-old dream for the people of the region. He said the new rail connectivity would strengthen links between Bahraich, Rupaidiha and Nepalganj and provide greater convenience to people on both sides of the border.

— Ministry of Railways (@RailMinIndia) August 31, 2026

New Opportunities for Aspirational District Bahraich

The completion of the gauge conversion project in the border area of aspirational district Bahraich is expected to give a major impetus to the region’s socio-economic development. Improved rail connectivity will facilitate greater movement of people and goods and promote trade, employment, tourism and social and cultural activities in the region.

The direct Broad Gauge connection will also provide better access to wider markets for local products and strengthen economic linkages between the border areas and major cities of Uttar Pradesh and beyond.

The improved rail infrastructure is expected to generate new opportunities for the people of the region and contribute to the overall development of Bahraich and adjoining areas.

Electrification of the rail section will enable the operation of electric locomotive-hauled trains, reducing dependence on diesel traction and helping lower carbon emissions. The initiative is aligned with Indian Railways’ efforts towards energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable railway operations.

Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw said that comprehensive planning is underway to strengthen the railway network across Uttar Pradesh, particularly the Purvanchal region. He said that seven major railway networks are being strengthened through the addition of third and fourth lines wherever double lines already exist. He highlighted the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Moradabad-Sitapur-Burhwal-Gonda-Gorakhpur network serving Purvanchal and said that the Delhi to Gonda section has already been approved.

He added that a major transformation in the State's rail connectivity would come with the development of high-speed rail connectivity. Referring to the proposed high-speed rail connectivity, Shri Vaishnaw said travel times would be significantly reduced. He said the Delhi-Agra journey would take 58 minutes, Delhi-Kanpur 1 hour 45 minutes, Delhi-Lucknow 2 hours 12 minutes and Delhi-Prayagraj around three hours. He added that Delhi-Varanasi would take about three and a half hours.

Shri Vaishnaw further highlighted that the proposed connectivity would eventually extend towards Patna. He said the 1,170-km journey between Delhi and Patna could be completed in around four and a half hours. He emphasized this would allow people to travel between major cities of Uttar Pradesh and other parts of North India within much shorter timeframes.

The completion of the Nepalganj Road-Nanpara-Bahraich rail section and the extension of long-distance train services mark an important milestone in strengthening rail connectivity in the border region. The project will not only connect the region more effectively with major cities across the country but will also create new avenues for socio-economic and cultural development.

headline: Digital India BHASHINI Division Organises BHASHINI शिल्पी in Nepal; Brings Developers Together to Build the Future of Language AI
fullText:
Ministry of Electronics & IT

Digital India BHASHINI Division Organises BHASHINI शिल्पी in Nepal; Brings Developers Together to Build the Future of Language AI

Interactive developer session explores how language technology can turn real-world challenges into inclusive, multilingual digital solutions

31 AUG 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, organised a BHASHINI शिल्पी session today at the Embassy of India, Kathmandu. The session brought together developers, technology practitioners and innovators from Nepal to explore the possibilities of building with Language AI.

Designed as an engaging and interactive platform for developers, students and innovators, BHASHINI शिल्पी goes beyond a conventional technology session to create a space where participants can learn, experiment, solve and build with Language AI. The session brings together ideas and technology, taking participants through the journey of developing, solving, scaling and innovating with BHASHINI, while encouraging them to explore real-world challenges, exchange ideas and discover new possibilities for creating inclusive, multilingual digital solutions. By putting participants at the centre of the conversation, BHASHINI शिल्पी aims to foster a growing community of builders who can use language technology to create solutions that are relevant to people, languages and communities.

The session featured live demonstrations, practical discussions and an open Question and Answer session, giving participants an opportunity to interact directly with the BHASHINI team, ask questions, clarify queries and explore possibilities for developing solutions with BHASHINI. Participants were introduced to BHASHINI APIs and developer resources and taken through the journey of Develop with BHASHINI, Solve with BHASHINI, Scale with BHASHINI and Innovate with BHASHINI, exploring how to get started, address challenges, take solutions from early ideas towards scale, and apply Language AI to real-world problem statements and use cases. A key highlight was the interactive “Innovate with BHASHINI” segment, where participants shared ideas and explored how BHASHINI could help turn problems into prototypes and scalable solutions.

Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, said:

"Language AI becomes truly meaningful when people can build with it to solve problems that matter. BHASHINI शिल्पी is about bringing developers, students and innovators into that journey, giving them the opportunity to experiment, ask questions, exchange ideas and turn real-world challenges into solutions. Our collaboration with Nepal is about building this ecosystem together and creating technology that works across languages and communities."

The enthusiastic participation, questions and open exchange of ideas reflected the growing interest among Nepal's technology and innovation community in leveraging Language AI to address diverse linguistic needs.

BHASHINI शिल्पी further strengthens the India-Nepal collaboration in language technology by creating opportunities for developers, academia and innovators to learn from each other, exchange ideas and co-create solutions for a more inclusive digital future.

The session captured the spirit of BHASHINI शिल्पी: not just showcasing what Language AI can do, but creating a space to ask questions, solve problems, share ideas and discover what we can build together.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India's national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI powers over 800 government websites, has enabled more than 9 billion cumulative AI inferences, processes over 24 million AI inferences daily, and supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, making Digital Public Infrastructure more accessible through Language AI.

headline: Collective commitment necessary to build resilient minds, strengthen connected campuses and advance student wellbeing, says Director, IIT Indore, Dr. Suhas S. Joshi
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Collective commitment necessary to build resilient minds, strengthen connected campuses and advance student wellbeing, says Director, IIT Indore, Dr. Suhas S. Joshi

Two-day capacity building workshop on positive mental health, resilience and wellbeing concludes at IIT Indore

31 AUG 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi

Director, IIT Indore, Dr. Suhas S. Joshi, today called for a collective commitment to build resilient minds, strengthen connected campuses and advance student wellbeing. He was speaking at the conclusion of the workshop on positive mental health, resilience and wellbeing, at the Indian Institute of Technology, Indore. He added that the key learnings gained from the Workshop must be translated into sustained institutional practices to promote positive mental health, resilience and holistic student wellbeing across campuses.

Titled “Samvardhan: From Academic Excellence to Sustainable Wellness”, the two-day capacity building Workshop was organised by the Department of Higher Education, Union Ministry of Education, in collaboration with IIT Indore.

The Workshop was aimed at strengthening institutional capacities for creating healthier, more supportive and connected higher education ecosystems. The programme brought together institutional leaders, faculty members, student affairs professionals, mental health experts, wardens, students, counsellors of participating institutions, to share their experiences and develop practical approaches for promoting student well-being.

The Workshop combined expert interaction, hands-on activities, participant brainstorming, recapitulation and feedback to facilitate experiential and collaborative learning. Experts and panelists were drawn from diverse areas of knowledge and professional experience, including psychiatry and mental health, nutrition and healthy lifestyles, Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS), learning disabilities and student support.

On the first day of the Workshop, several sessions were organised on the psychosocial landscape of higher education institutions from robust policies to sustainable practices, institutional wellbeing initiatives, social belonging and connected campuses, early identification and facilitation of interventions, life-skills-based peer mentoring, and prevention of lifestyle-related conditions.

The second day focused on providing hands-on experience in identifying flag signs, specific learning disabilities, prevention of substance use, hostel ecosystems, collaborative living spaces and mentoring networks. The Workshop culminated with the development of institutional/university wellbeing indicators, final recommendations and action plans by the participating institutions.

The Workshop was organised under the Teacher Connect Programme of Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme (MMTTP), for the central and west regions. It brought together 94 participants from 21 Higher Education Institutions across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Punjab and Madhya Pradesh.

headline: Dr. Jitendra Singh Calls for Wider Awareness about Rs 1 Lakh Crore RDI Fund Among Stakeholders to Ensure Right Beneficiaries Avail of Support
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Dr. Jitendra Singh Calls for Wider Awareness about Rs 1 Lakh Crore RDI Fund Among Stakeholders to Ensure Right Beneficiaries Avail of Support

Greater Outreach Needed to Ensure RDI Fund Reaches Technology and Research Stakeholders and Contributes to National Economic Growth

Technology Development Board Must Evolve as a Strategic Enabler of India’s Future Technology Sectors: Dr. Jitendra Singh

01 SEP 2026 4:35PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh today called for greater awareness and outreach about Rs 1 Lakh Crore “Research, Development and Innovation Fund” (RDI Fund) among stakeholders so that the right kind of applicants understand its purpose, eligibility and the process for availing support.

Addressing the 30th Foundation Day of the Technology Development Board (TDB), Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the focus should be on creating awareness about the spirit behind the RDI Fund, the stakeholders and companies eligible for support, and how they can avail of the funding. He observed that the large number of applications being received also indicated a need for greater clarity and outreach about the purpose of the Fund.

The Minister said that thousands of applications are being received, including from applicants who do not appear to understand the nature and purpose of the RDI Fund. He cautioned against the perception that the Fund is simply another source of finance or a conventional loan facility, stressing the need to ensure that there is no misunderstanding about the funding process.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the RDI Fund is intended to support technology development and research in a manner that contributes to the progress of science and research and makes these activities part of the overall growth of the national economy. He called for efforts to ensure that stakeholders understand the spirit and intended purpose of the Fund so that its benefits reach the appropriate beneficiaries.

The Minister emphasised that the funding process is already transparent and has proper safeguards in place, even though the government is open to suggestions for further safeguards wherever feasible. He said, there is scope to further increase outreach and awareness. He said that better awareness would help the right kind of people avail of the support in the interest of scientific and research progress and its contribution to national economic growth.

Referring to the role of TDB, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Board must also play a role in educating those for whom such initiatives are meant. He stressed that while technology and policy frameworks are changing rapidly, the mindset of stakeholders also needs to change accordingly.

The Minister said that TDB was created with the vision of ensuring that technologies do not remain confined to laboratories but are translated into products, solutions and enterprises that can bring ease of living to citizens, provide livelihoods and contribute to the overall economy of the country. He said that the occasion of the 30th Foundation Day was an opportunity to look back at how far this spirit had been carried forward.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that over the last 12 years this spirit had been vindicated and credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi with placing science, technology and innovation high on the government agenda. He described the period as a decade of scientific renaissance in the country, highlighting achievements in science and technology and India's ability to deliver cost-effective successes.

Emphasising the importance of changing mindsets, the Minister said that continuous learning and curiosity would be essential to keeping pace with rapid technological developments. He stressed that stakeholders must make the best use of the enabling environment provided by policymakers.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the growth of the start-up ecosystem and called for prevailing myths about entrepreneurship to be dispelled. He noted that start-ups are not confined to Bengaluru or Hyderabad, that more than 50 per cent are from smaller towns, and that entrepreneurship is not necessarily restricted to young people. He also highlighted the participation of women in the ecosystem.

The Minister underlined the importance of openness to private-sector participation and said that this approach had been followed in sectors including space, biotechnology and the nuclear sector. He stressed that resource pooling and integration among institutions and stakeholders are important for strengthening the ecosystem.

Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated TDB's role in supporting the journey from laboratory to market and noted that the Board had, in practice, extended support beyond narrowly defined domains. He referred to examples including Skyroot and BotLab, and said that moving beyond a conventional bureaucratic approach had enabled TDB to become an important part of the emerging technology ecosystem.

The Minister also highlighted the need for a culture of philanthropy in research. He said that funding research that ultimately contributes to the well-being of mankind should also be recognised as a form of worship and called for such a culture to be created.

Looking ahead, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that TDB should support technology development both in the early phase and at the later stage. He noted that the RDI Fund is offering support at a later stage at TRL4 level and that TDB is the first to roll out its proposals.

He said that TDB has set up a model of public-private transition and technology self-reliance which could become an important pillar of India's economy and contribute not only to India but also to the Global South. He further observed that strengthening India's technological capabilities would also strengthen the country's geopolitical status in the Global South and across the world.

The Minister said that the first thirty years of TDB were about building the bridge between the laboratory and the market, while the next thirty years should focus on building global technology champions from India. The accompanying address similarly emphasised the need to move from ideas to innovation, from innovation to industry and towards a truly developed India by 2047.

Dr. Jitendra Singh extended his good wishes to TDB and called for the institution to continue building on its role in technology development, public-private transition and technology self-reliance.

The Minister emphasised that the funding process is already transparent and has proper safeguards in place, even though the government is open to suggestions for further safeguards wherever feasible. He said, there is scope to further increase outreach and awareness. He said that better awareness would help the right kind of people avail of the support in the interest of scientific and research progress and its contribution to national economic growth.

Referring to the role of TDB, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Board must also play a role in educating those for whom such initiatives are meant. He stressed that while technology and policy frameworks are changing rapidly, the mindset of stakeholders also needs to change accordingly.

The Minister said that TDB was created with the vision of ensuring that technologies do not remain confined to laboratories but are translated into products, solutions and enterprises that can bring ease of living to citizens, provide livelihoods and contribute to the overall economy of the country. He said that the occasion of the 30th Foundation Day was an opportunity to look back at how far this spirit had been carried forward.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that over the last 12 years this spirit had been vindicated and credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi with placing science, technology and innovation high on the government agenda. He described the period as a decade of scientific renaissance in the country, highlighting achievements in science and technology and India's ability to deliver cost-effective successes.

Emphasising the importance of changing mindsets, the Minister said that continuous learning and curiosity would be essential to keeping pace with rapid technological developments. He stressed that stakeholders must make the best use of the enabling environment provided by policymakers.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the growth of the start-up ecosystem and called for prevailing myths about entrepreneurship to be dispelled. He noted that start-ups are not confined to Bengaluru or Hyderabad, that more than 50 per cent are from smaller towns, and that entrepreneurship is not necessarily restricted to young people. He also highlighted the participation of women in the ecosystem.

The Minister underlined the importance of openness to private-sector participation and said that this approach had been followed in sectors including space, biotechnology and the nuclear sector. He stressed that resource pooling and integration among institutions and stakeholders are important for strengthening the ecosystem.

Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated TDB's role in supporting the journey from laboratory to market and noted that the Board had, in practice, extended support beyond narrowly defined domains. He referred to examples including Skyroot and BotLab, and said that moving beyond a conventional bureaucratic approach had enabled TDB to become an important part of the emerging technology ecosystem.

The Minister also highlighted the need for a culture of philanthropy in research. He said that funding research that ultimately contributes to the well-being of mankind should also be recognised as a form of worship and called for such a culture to be created.

Looking ahead, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that TDB should support technology development both in the early phase and at the later stage. He noted that the RDI Fund is offering support at a later stage at TRL4 level and that TDB is the first to roll out its proposals.

He said that TDB has set up a model of public-private transition and technology self-reliance which could become an important pillar of India's economy and contribute not only to India but also to the Global South. He further observed that strengthening India's technological capabilities would also strengthen the country's geopolitical status in the Global South and across the world.

The Minister said that the first thirty years of TDB were about building the bridge between the laboratory and the market, while the next thirty years should focus on building global technology champions from India. The accompanying address similarly emphasised the need to move from ideas to innovation, from innovation to industry and towards a truly developed India by 2047.

Dr. Jitendra Singh extended his good wishes to TDB and called for the institution to continue building on its role in technology development, public-private transition and technology self-reliance.

headline: NHAI Receives Overwhelming Response from Bidders for Construction of Coastal Corridor from Rameshwar to Paradeep in Odisha
fullText:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways

NHAI Receives Overwhelming Response from Bidders for Construction of Coastal Corridor from Rameshwar to Paradeep in Odisha

01 SEP 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi

National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has received an overwhelming response from the bidders for the implementation of 160 km long Access Controlled Greenfield Coastal National Highway from Rameshwar to Paradeep in Odisha. Bids were invited by NHAI for construction of the project in two packages and both packages received encouraging participation from the bidders.

The 79.4 km long 4 lane access-controlled Rameshwar to Konark Package-I of the project received 10 bids, and 80.7 km long 2-lane with Paved Shoulder Konark to Paradeep Package-II received seven bids, reflecting robust competition and keen interest from the participants. The project will be awarded on Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM).

The new coastal Highway from Rameshwar to Paradeep project was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs in June 2026 with a combined total capital cost of Rs.8,300.79 crores. During construction, the project is expected to have a potential to generate 53.6 Lakhs direct man-days and 67 lakh indirect man-days of employment.

With a design speed of 100 km/hour, the project will provide direct & fast connectivity to key tourist places like Sri Jagganath Temple, Puri Beach & Konark Sun Temple and help to reduce travel time between Rameshawar and Paradeep by about 2 hours and 30 minutes.

Rameshwar-Paradeep section of Coastal Highway will offer an alternate route for NH-16 & NH-316 and improve connectivity to Puri, Konark, Paradeep Port, upcoming Puri International Airport, facilitate smooth transportation to developing ports like Astarang and Subarnarekha as well as provide connectivity to Khurda, Puri, Kendrapada and Jagatsinghpur districts in Odisha.

The existing NH-16 is part of the Golden Quadrilateral and passes through major towns of Khordha, Bhubaneswar and Cuttack. Whereas NH-316 connects Bhubaneswar to Puri and further extends towards Satapada and Konark. The current sections along Puri–Satapada and Puri–Konark stretches has nearly 40% ribbon development along the corridor with high local commuter traffic, making the corridor unsuitable for high-speed long-distance vehicular movement.

The Rameshwar-Paradeep corridor will provide faster access-controlled connectivity, reduce fuel consumption, carbon emissions & vehicle operating costs, while lowering logistics costs and supporting economic growth across the region.

headline: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reviews Progress of Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana
fullText:

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reviews Progress of Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana

Average score of 100 Dhan-Dhaanya districts improves from 22.54 in April to 38.85 in July 2026

Focus on outcome-based monitoring, convergence of 36 schemes and ensuring benefits reach farmers

01 SEP 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today reviewed the progress of the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY) at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. The review focused on accelerating implementation in the 100 identified districts, strengthening convergence among schemes, improving district-level performance and ensuring that interventions translate into measurable outcomes and tangible benefits for farmers.

During the review, the Minister was apprised of the progress of PM-DDKY through the scheme’s dashboard, including district-wise performance, District Action Plans, field monitoring by Central Nodal Officers (CNOs), financial progress, capacity building, convergence of schemes and mechanisms being developed to track beneficiary-level outcomes.

Data-driven monitoring of 100 districts

PM-DDKY aims to accelerate agricultural development in 100 districts identified on the basis of low agricultural productivity, low cropping intensity and low agricultural credit disbursement.

The scheme focuses on six key objectives: increasing agricultural productivity; promoting crop diversification and sustainable agricultural practices; enhancing post-harvest storage capacity; improving irrigation infrastructure; enabling greater access to short- and long-term agricultural credit; and improving governance and service delivery.

The scheme is being implemented through the convergence of 36 Central schemes of 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private-sector participation.

A total of 121 indicators, comprising 74 output indicators and 47 outcome indicators, have been identified across the 36 schemes for monitoring progress against annual targets. District performance on output indicators is ranked every month through the PM-DDKY dashboard, while outcome indicators will facilitate assessment of progress against the baseline.

The average score of the 100 districts across the six objectives increased from 22.54 in April 2026 to 38.85 in July 2026, an improvement of 16.31 points.

Objective-wise performance also recorded improvement during the period. The average score for agricultural productivity increased from 2.53 in April to 6.70 in July; crop diversification and sustainable agricultural practices from 5.60 to 8.65; post-harvest storage capacity from 2.61 to 3.82; irrigation infrastructure from 1.65 to 4.20; access to agricultural credit from 2.81 to 5.59; and governance and service delivery from 7.94 to 10.33.

All 100 districts have uploaded District Action Plans

The review noted that all 100 districts have uploaded their District Action Plans (DAPs) and feedback has been provided on the DAPs of all 100 districts.

All 100 districts have submitted data against output indicators up to July 2026, while all 100 districts have also submitted outcome-indicator data for the financial year 2025-26.

Committees have been constituted at the State, District and national levels for review and monitoring. Central Nodal Officers are also undertaking regular field-level monitoring of implementation.

Focus on outcomes and benefits reaching farmers

The review emphasised strengthening the monitoring framework to move beyond tracking activities and expenditure towards measuring outcomes and the actual benefits reaching farmers.

The Financial Progress Module of the PM-DDKY dashboard was implemented on 31 August 2026. A Beneficiary Progress Module is targeted for implementation by mid-September 2026 to enable systematic capture of beneficiary-level progress.

The strengthened dashboard will also facilitate consolidation of investments and interventions undertaken through Central schemes, State schemes and other sources in the Dhan-Dhaanya districts.

This will enable a comprehensive assessment of the resources deployed, activities undertaken, farmers benefited and outcomes achieved across the identified districts.

Capacity building of farmers and extension workers

Capacity development is an important component of PM-DDKY implementation. During January to July 2026, a total of 6,90,530 farmers and 88,961 extension workers were trained in various skills.

In addition, 2,20,683 farmers and extension workers were trained in natural farming during the period.

Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) are being utilised as technical partners for capacity development and field-level interventions, strengthening the agricultural extension system and facilitating dissemination of improved agricultural practices among farmers.

Strengthening convergence and partnerships

The review also focused on strengthening convergence among the 36 Central schemes of 11 Ministries and Departments, State schemes and private-sector interventions.

The Department of Public Enterprises has included adoption of PM-DDKY districts for CSR activities by Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) for 2026-27 and 2027-28, providing an additional avenue for supporting development interventions in the identified districts.

The monitoring mechanism is being strengthened to capture such convergence and investments, enabling assessment of the combined impact of interventions being implemented in the Dhan-Dhaanya districts.

PM-DDKY to complete one year in October

PM-DDKY was approved by the Union Cabinet on 16 July 2025 and officially launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister on 11 October 2025. The PM-DDKY dashboard was activated in the last week of October 2025, with monthly output-indicator rankings commencing from November 2025.

As the scheme approaches completion of its first year in October 2026, a programme is being planned to highlight the progress and performance of the 100 Dhan-Dhaanya districts. Progress will also be showcased during Rabi and regional conferences.

The review also considered convening a meeting of the National Executive Committee under the chairmanship of the Agriculture Minister and strengthening farmer participation through the proposed nomination of two progressive farmers in each District Dhan-Dhaanya Committee.

headline: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj launched fisheries Infrastructure projects worth Rs 36.49 Crore
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj launched fisheries Infrastructure projects worth Rs 36.49 Crore

Major Focus on Strengthening Fisheries Infrastructure to Boost the Fisheries Value Chain and create better livelihoods opportunities

01 SEP 2026 4:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government of India in collaboration with Government of Puducherry has organized the launch of Fisheries Infrastructure Project under PMMSY and Multi-Dimensional Capacity Building Conclave for Co-operative Led Seaweed Farming under Blue Economy on 1st September 2026, at Kamarajar Manimadapam, Puducherry to strengthen fisheries infrastructure, promote sustainable livelihood opportunities for coastal communities, enhance value chain efficiencies and accelerate the development through a cooperative-led approach.

The Outreach Programme was graced by the august presence of Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Shri K. Kailashnathan, Hon'ble Lieutenant Governor, Puducherry, Thiru N. Rangasamy, Hon'ble Chief Minister, Puducherry, Thiru A. Anbalagan, Hon'ble Speaker, Puducherry Legislative Assembly, Shri G. N. S. Rajasekaran, Hon'ble Agriculture Minister, Puducherry, Shri A. Namassivayam, Hon'ble Home Minister, Puducherry, A. John Kumaradhas, Hon'ble Chief Minister's Adviser, V. P. Sivakolundhu, Hon'ble Civil Supplies Minister, Puducherry, Shri V. Vaithilingam, Hon'ble Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), Puducherry, Shri S. Selvaganabathy, Hon'ble Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha), Puducherry, Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Government of India and Dr Sharat Chauhan, Chief Secretary, Government of Puducherry.

The event also witnessed the participation of fish farmers and fishers including women fish farmers and fishers in person, along with officials from the Department of Fisheries, GoI, Government of Puducherry, NFDB, and representatives from fisheries value chain stakeholders. The event also witnessed participation of fishers including women fish farmers, Fisheries Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), fisheries research institutes and representatives of fisheries value-chain stakeholders.

Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon'ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, inaugurated the three projects, namely the upgradation of Thengaithittu Fishing Harbour, the Nallavadu Fish Landing Centre under PMMSY, and the Advanced Centre for Innovation and Capacity Development in Seaweed Farming at Karaikal, and stated that these are not merely infrastructure projects but long-term assets that will strengthen the livelihoods of fishing communities. Highlighting the transformative impact of flagship initiatives such as PMMSY, FIDF and PM-MKSSY, he noted that India's fish production has increased from 95.7 lakh tonnes in 2013-14 to 197.7 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while fisheries exports have grown substantially over the period. Emphasizing the vast untapped potential of India's marine resources, he noted that the Government has issued rules for fishing in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and guidelines for high sea fisheries, introduced Access Pass and Letters of Authorization, and accorded priority to the cooperatives of fishers and women and self-help groups. He encouraged fishers to adopt deep-sea fishing, particularly targeting high-value species such as tuna, and informed that enhanced support for deep-sea fishing vessels would be provided under the upcoming PMMSY 2.0. The Minister highlighted the growing potential of seaweed farming as a sustainable livelihood avenue for fisherwomen. The Minister also announced the Government of India’s commitment to support the efforts of the Government of Puducherry for the Development of the Mahe Fishing Harbour project, estimated at about ₹67 crore and requested the Government of Puducherry to formulate and submit the proposal expeditiously for consideration.

During the conclave, The Union Minister launched fisheries Infrastructure projects worth Rs 36.49 Crore including ₹18.94 crore Fish Landing Centre at Nallavadu, the ₹15.63 crore upgradation of Puducherry Fishing Harbour, and the ₹1.92 crore Advanced Centre for Innovation and Capacity Development in Seaweed Farming at Karaika.

Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel, Hon'ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj, emphasized the crucial role of the fisheries sector in strengthening India's economy, food security and employment generation, noting that the welfare and prosperity of fishing communities remain a key priority of the Government under the leadership of the Hon'ble Prime Minister. Highlighting the vast potential of marine fisheries, inland fisheries and seaweed cultivation in Puducherry, he stated that initiatives under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) are transforming the sector into a modern economic activity while creating new livelihood opportunities for fishers. He underscored the importance of seaweed farming as a future-oriented activity and noted that the projects being launched would enhance fisheries infrastructure, improve fishers' incomes and support the growth of the Blue Economy in the Union Territory. He also lauded the role of fisherwomen in successfully adopting seaweed cultivation and reiterated the Government's commitment to expanding the sector through technology-driven interventions and capacity building.

Shri K. Kailashnathan, Hon’ble Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry, highlighted the pivotal role of the fisheries sector in India's economic growth, food security and employment generation, and underscored the Government of India's strong commitment to the welfare of fishing communities under the leadership of the Hon'ble Prime Minister. He noted that fisheries projects worth ₹350.26 crore have been implemented in Puducherry between 2021 and 2024-25, including ₹296.43 crore as Central assistance. He further informed that projects worth ₹349.14 crore have been planned in Puducherry under PMMSY over the next five years. Highlighting key initiatives launched during the event and stated that it would enhance fisheries infrastructure, generate employment, increase fishers' incomes and transform Puducherry into a modern hub of the Blue Economy. He also emphasized the potential of seaweed farming in creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for fisherwomen and strengthening the coastal economy.

Shri N. Rangasamy, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Puducherry, highlighted that the Government of India, under the leadership of the Hon'ble Prime Minister, has been implementing several initiatives to enhance fisheries production, increase exports and improve the livelihoods of fisherfolk. He noted that nearly ₹130 crore has been allocated for the fisheries sector and emphasized the benefits being extended to fishers through diesel subsidy, boat subsidy, fishing ban period assistance, old-age support and educational assistance. He further announced that the Government would provide full financial support for the education of children from fishing families, from school to higher education. Underscoring the importance of the fisheries sector in strengthening the economy and ensuring nutritional security, he urged fishers to make optimum use of the infrastructure being created under various schemes, including PMMSY, and stressed the need for its proper maintenance to secure long-term benefits for the fishing community.

Puducherry is emerging as a model for sustainable and infrastructure-led fisheries development under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). Blessed with rich marine resources and a vibrant fishing community, the Union Territory has witnessed significant investments in modern fisheries infrastructure, including the upgradation of the Thengaithittu Fishing Harbour and the establishment of a state-of-the-art Fish Landing Centre at Nallavadu. These facilities have enhanced fish handling, berthing, auctioning and safety arrangements, benefiting thousands of fishers and over 600 fishing families in the coastal region.

Further strengthening fisheries sector, the Government of India has adopted a cluster-based approach under PMMSY by notifying Karaikal as a Fishing Harbour Cluster and undertaking the development of a Smart and Integrated Fishing Harbour at Karaikal with an investment of ₹119.94 crore. The project will provide modern infrastructure for safe vessel berthing, hygienic fish handling and efficient fish marketing, while improving operational efficiency across the fisheries value chain. The integrated cluster approach will also promote the growth of Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs) and fisheries cooperatives through enhanced access to infrastructure, finance, technology, value addition and markets, enabling collective participation across the value chain, unlocking Puducherry's untapped fisheries potential, increasing fishers' incomes and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for coastal communities.
